questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “no improvement”.**

Tunnels (is built) to connect houses and places of worship whereas innovative trick doors were attached to the underground cities.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__were built__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Since the sentence is in past tense, we need past tense in the improvement part.
 
• If the subject is plural, we need a plural verb after it and if the subject is singular, we need a singular verb after it.
 
• **'Tunnels' **is **plural**, so **a plural verb** should be used **after it.**
 
• 'was/ were + V₃' is used in passive voice.

**Thus, the sentence becomes: ***Tunnels **were built** to connect houses and places of worship whereas innovative trick doors were attached to the underground cities.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “no improvement”.**

I understood that we (is influenced) by what we see, what we hear.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**are influenced**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **What is understood is a generalized statement**. So it should be in present tense.
 
• 'is/are + V₃' is used in passive voice.
 
• If the receiver of the action is emphasized upon, then the sentence is in passive voice.

**Thus, the sentence becomes: ***I understood that we **are influenced** by what we see, what we hear.*

• **But also: 'but also' **is used after **'not only'. **It is used for emphasizing the fact that there is something more to add.

• **Or: **You use or to link two or more alternatives.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Ram loves Sita.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sita is loved by Ram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the **active** voice and '**Ram**' is the subject and '**Sita**' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into **passive** voice, the subject 'Sita' of the **active** voice becomes the object, the object '**Ram**' becomes the subject.
 
• The active format "**V₁**" should be converted into the passive format "**is/are** + V₂".
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the **present indefinite** tense.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:

 PASSIVE CONVERSION
 
 

 Present Simple
 He plays football

 Football is played by him

 He is/am/are playing football

 Football is being played by him

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.**

Incumbent
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Required__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Incumbent: **necessary

 **Example: ***It is incumbent upon (= necessary for) all of us to create a safe community.*
 
• **Increase:** to (make something) become larger in amount or size

 **Example: **Incidents of armed robbery have increased over the last few years.
 
• **Redundant: **(especially of a word, phrase, etc.) unnecessary because it is more than is needed

 **Example: **Changes in technology may mean that once-valued skills are now redundant.
 
• **Choice: **If there is a choice of things, there are several of them and you can choose the one you want.

 **Example: **It's available in a choice of colours.
 
• **Required:** essential, needed, or necessary

 **Example:** *eight editions were published, each required reading for trainees.*
 
• Thus, required is the synonym of incumbent

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.**

Imitate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__ape__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The meanings of the words are;
 
 
• **Imitate:** copy or simulate

 **Example: **Some of the younger pop bands try to imitate their musical heroes from the past.
 
• **Reverse:** make (something) the opposite of what it was.

 **Example: **The new manager hoped to reverse the decline in the company's fortunes.
 
• **Ape:** imitate (someone or something), especially in an absurd or unthinking way.

 **Example: **He called the new building unoriginal and said that it merely aped the classical traditions.
 
• **Clash:** a violent confrontation.

 **Example: ***Students clashed with police after demonstrations at five universities.*
 
• **Repulse:** cause to feel intense distaste and aversion.

 **Example: **The enemy attack was quickly repulsed.
 
 
 
• Thus, we can see from the meanings of the given words that **option 2** is the correct answer since the verb **ape **means to **imitate**.

• The meanings of the words are:
 
 
• **Abetting:** encourage or assist (someone) to do something wrong, in particular, to commit a crime.
 
• **Begging:** ask someone earnestly or humbly for something.
 
• **Caging:** imprisoning
 
• **Daring:** bold
 
 
 
• Your self-esteem is how you feel about yourself. For example, if you have low self-esteem, you do not like yourself, you do not think that you are a valuable person, and therefore you do not behave confidently.
 
• Thus option 2 fits here conveying the meaning that self-esteem demands not to beg for something which can be earned.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

In June 2017, an anodyne footnote to the Bank of Baroda’s (bob) quarter results mentioned a (1)/fine levied by the South African Reserve Bank (SARB), (2)/headquartered in Pretoria. (3)/No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The error lies in part 1 of the sentence as the noun 'quarter' is incorrect and must be replaced with the adjective 'quarterly'. Here we need an adjective to qualify the noun 'results'.
 
• **Quarter: **one of four equal parts of something
 
• A quarterly event happens four times a year, at intervals of three months.
 
• **It should read as:** '*In June 2017, an anodyne footnote to the Bank of Baroda’s (bob) **quarterly results** mentioned a..'*

questions.question:

• The error lies in part 2 of the sentence as the verb 'decided' in past tense is incorrect. It must be in participle form 'deciding' or the preposition 'to' should be written and the form of the verb should be transitive 'decide.'
